Customer is interested in a 6-week pilot with VPC private control plane and SOC2 requirements; main concerns were latency vs cost, data residency, and how alerts surface false positives.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-14
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Sofia (Redwood SE), Alex (Echo PM), Priya (Echo Eng), Mark (Echo CISO)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll do a quick 45-ish minute run through of the evaluation and then time for Q and A, Sofia will take the demo.
[00:08] Alex: Great thanks Jordan, excited — we set aside time to see how Redwood handles prompt drift and regression alerts, mostly want to understand how A/B compares work at scale.
[00:14] Sofia: Awesome, quick agenda: I'll show the Console prompt-sets, how to attach metrics and pass/fail criteria, then Optimize suggestions for batching/quantization, and finally a live A/B compare run.
[00:27] Priya: Sounds good, our concerns are p95 latency under load and false positive alerts — we run medical triage so hallucinations are a big no no.
[00:34] Mark: Security note: we need to confirm KMS-backed encryption and audit logs are included in the pilot.
[00:40] Jordan: Yep we'll cover that — we have a SOC2 pack, plus options for private VPC deployment, sharing link after this.

--- Demo start ---
[02:05] Sofia: I'm in the Console now — landing page shows prompt-sets, you can import a CSV or build them inline. For this demo I uploaded a small triage prompt set (note: demo data scrubbed). Each prompt has expected outputs and a comparator — could be string match, regex, or semantic similarity.
[02:39] Alex: Quick question, does the comparator use embeddings or fuzzy text match by default?
[02:44] Sofia: By default semantic similarity uses Redwood embeddings with cosine, but you can toggle to lexical or custom eval hooks if you want. The console shows per-example baseline responses and a historical distribution.
[03:10] Priya: How do you handle tokenization differences across model variants? Our pipeline uses different model families.
[03:16] Sofia: Good question — we store canonical normalized texts, and the evals are model-agnostic when using semantic sim, we also show token counts and estimated unit cost per model variant so you can compare latency/cost tradeoffs.
[04:02] Jordan: We also surface estimated per-token cost and a quick projection for the pilot based on your traffic shape.

[05:00] Sofia: Moving to regression alerts: you define a metric — e.g., semantic similarity 0.85 threshold or pass rate 98% — and set the aggregation window, sensitivity, and who to notify. The UI shows a preview of alert windows using historical data.
[05:28] Alex: When an alert fires what do we get? Email? Pager? Slack?
[05:33] Sofia: All of the above — Slack and webhook are common. We also attach a sample failing prompt set and a diff view for side-by-side model outputs. There's an option to attach request traces and the KV cache snapshot to help debugging.
[05:52] Priya: KV cache? you mean key-value cache for generation?
[05:56] Sofia: Yeah, sometimes the auto-transcribe reads it as K V cache, but it's the generation KV cache. We can attach that context as well for repro.

[07:10] Sofia: Now I'll trigger a synthetic regression — switch model variant from rdl-3-small -> rdl-3-mid and show A/B.
[07:22] Sofia: Starting the A/B compare job: select baseline model, candidate model, prompt-set, split traffic, choose metrics (semantic sim, length, safety hits) and hit run.
[07:35] Jordan: Note: you can run A/B on live traffic (sampled) or simulated replay. For pilot we recommend replay first to avoid user-facing regressions.
[08:05] Alex: Can we schedule recurring A/B runs against production?
[08:08] Sofia: Yes, cron-style scheduling is supported and you can attach alerting policies to the A/B evaluation as well.

[09:00] [Sofia runs job, UI updates — several loading indicators, small chatty commentary omitted]
[09:30] Sofia: Results are in — here's a waterfall: baseline pass rate 98.7%, candidate 95.1%, semantic sim delta -0.12, safety hits +2. There are three prompts with large deltas flagged.
[09:48] Priya: Show me the diffs — which prompts regressed?
[09:52] Sofia: Prompt 12 looks like it truncated the clinical context and hallucinates an outcome, we attach the request trace and model tokenization snapshot.
[10:10] Alex: This is useful — can we auto-open a JIRA or push to our bug tracker from the alert?
[10:15] Sofia: Yep there's integrations — JIRA, PagerDuty, Opsgenie, or custom webhook. You can templated payloads so the issue includes the failed examples and links to the Console session.

[12:05] Priya: How often do you see false positives with semantic sim? Sometimes wording changes but correctness is fine.
[12:12] Sofia: We see that; recommended practice is to combine multiple signals — semantic sim + response-length + safety classifier. Also set a higher aggregation window — e.g., 5% sustained drop rather than single-sample threshold. We also support human-in-loop labels to re-train the comparator.

[14:20] Jordan: On the Optimize side, the system will suggest batching parameters and quantization profiles based on observed sequence length distribution. For Echo you might get suggestions to enable int8 per certain model families to save 30-40% cost per token.
[14:44] Priya: Any caveats for medical language? Quantization sometimes affects tokenization, we worry about subtle artifacts.
[14:52] Sofia: Absolutely — Optimize will flag potential quality regressions after quantization by running the prompt set and verifying pass rates, and you can set safety margins to disable a profile if regressions exceed N examples.

[16:00] Mark: From security: how is encryption at rest handled for prompt-sets and stored traces?
[16:06] Sofia: By default data at rest is encrypted, and for Private we support customer-managed KMS/HSM. Audit logs are retained per policy and we can route them to your logging endpoint inside the VPC.
[16:25] Mark: And access control? RBAC?
[16:28] Jordan: RBAC via SSO (SAML/OIDC) with roles and token-scoped access for APIs. Everything's logged with request IDs.

[18:30] Sofia: Back to alerts — configuration UI includes a learn mode where the alert will only log candidate events for N days so you can tune thresholds without noisy pings. Alex: That's appealing.
[18:48] Alex: How do you handle drift detection vs transient blips?
[18:52] Sofia: We model baseline distributions and use EWMA + outlier detection. For production we recommend a tiered approach: low sensitivity for auto-alerts, high sensitivity for internal dashboards.

[21:10] Sofia: Quick note about the API: all of this is available via REST/SDK — you can programmatically kick off A/B runs, attach custom metrics, and pull diffs. I'll switch to the API tab to show a cURL example.
[21:31] Sofia: cURL snippet: POST /v1/evals/ab-run with payload includes baseline_model, candidate_model, prompt_set_id, metric_config. Response returns job_id and web link.
[21:48] Priya: For the pilot we prefer SDK and replay tooling so we can integrate with our internal test harness.
[21:55] Sofia: We can provide a Python SDK snippet and a small replay harness that replays traffic from a CSV to the eval engine.

[25:10] Jordan: Pricing note — pilot uses hosted eval credits; we can move to Dedicated or Private for the pilot depending on your security needs. There's an option to reserve capacity for evaluation windows so A/B runs don't contend with serving.
[25:30] Mark: If we do Private deployment, does the Console still reach your control plane? We prefer a private control plane option.
[25:36] Jordan: Private has a customer-managed control plane within your VPC or air-gapped on-prem option for extreme cases; the Console can be hosted in your VPC and talk to private infra.

[27:00] Alex: About false positives again — can we attach sample human labels to tune the comparator?
[27:06] Sofia: Yes, human labels are first-class. You can attach label sets to prompts, and overwrite baselines so the system learns from labeled ground truth.

[29:22] Sofia: I'm going to show a short demo of alert configuration — setting sensitivity, excluded prompts, and automated remediation rules. For example, auto-fallback to a more conservative model variant when pass rate dips below 95%.
[29:45] Priya: So automatic rollback is supported?
[29:48] Sofia: It can trigger a routing policy to shift x% traffic to a fallback model or route to a slower but safer model. There's also staged rollouts and canary tests.

[32:10] Alex: How long does a full A/B run take for a 5k prompt set?
[32:15] Sofia: Depends on model and whether replay or live sampling — replay on Dedicated infra could finish in tens of minutes, on hosted it might take a few hours if you’re running large models concurrently. We show ETA in the UI.

[34:05] Priya: How do we get the raw diffs and artifacts for compliance?
[34:10] Sofia: You can export a zip containing request traces, model outputs, tokenization snapshots, and the comparator metrics. For Private, exports can be stored in your S3 bucket.

[36:00] Jordan: Quick recap — we showed prompt-sets, semantic comparator, regression alerts with integrations, A/B compare flow, and Optimize suggestions. Proposed pilot: 6 weeks, replay-based A/B validations weekly, one - two scheduled alert tiers, and a security review.
[36:20] Alex: That sounds right. What does success look like for us? Reduced hallucination incidents by x% and maintain p95 latency under 400ms.
[36:28] Jordan: We'll map success criteria in the SOW and include measurement details.

[38:10] Mark: I'll need SOC2 docs and the data flow diagram before legal signs off.
[38:15] Jordan: I'll put that in the next steps and share the secure link.

[40:00] Sofia: Any other product questions?
[40:07] Priya: Is there a way to simulate token-level noise to stress-test the comparator?
[40:12] Sofia: Yes, the replay harness supports perturbations and we ship a small fuzzing tool to apply permutations.

[42:30] Alex: If we wanted to extend the pilot to include model fine-tuning, does Redwood support that?
[42:36] Sofia: We don't host fine-tuning as a managed step yet in the hosted product, but you can use evaluation hooks to validate fine-tuned models and Redwood can serve self-hosted fine-tuned artifacts via the Private deployment.

[44:00] Jordan: Ok we'll close with next steps — I'll email the Pilot SOW template and pricing, Sofia will add the demo prompt set and SDK snippets, Priya provide traffic, Mark will request security docs.
[44:20] Alex: Good, thanks everyone, the diffs view and alert attachments look like they'll map well to our current QA flow.
[44:28] Priya: Thanks, really helpful.
[44:32] Mark: Thanks all.
[44:40] Jordan: Thanks, we'll follow up with links and action items within 24 hours.

End of transcript.
